summary: The Zeekr 7X is a mid-size electric SUV that Australian reviewers treat as the most complete Tesla Model Y alternative on price, with an 800V platform, a 615km WLTP Long Range grade and a cabin most testers rate above the Volkswagen ID.4 GTX and Kia EV5 GT-Line for the money. Reviewers agree on the packaging, charging speed and equipment, but split hard on which grade to buy: CarExpert and Chasing Cars both criticise the top grades' adaptive air suspension for bouncing at freeway speeds and prefer the steel-sprung Long Range RWD, while Chasing Cars still rated the Performance AWD 8/10. Recurring complaints are unreliable powered doors, almost everything buried in the 16-inch touchscreen, weak air-conditioning on hot days, no spare wheel, and the unknown resale of a brand that has only sold cars here since 2024.
pros: The $63,900 Long Range RWD is the range sweet spot: 95kWh usable for 615km WLTP, more range than a Tesla Model Y Long Range AWD ($68,900) or any Kia EV5 and for less money, with The Beep recording 500-550km at a sustained 110km/h

800V architecture with a 450kW DC peak on the RWD and Long Range and 22kW AC charging across the range - Chasing Cars timed the Performance AWD's 10-80 per cent DC charge at 16 minutes, and 22kW AC is double or triple the 7-11kW most rivals accept

Rated to tow 2000kg braked on every variant, against 1588kg for a Tesla Model Y, 1250kg for a Kia EV5 and 750kg for a BYD Sealion 7 Premium, with a 539L boot, 1978L seats folded and a 62L frunk on a 2900mm wheelbase

Ownership costs are unusually well defined for a new brand: five-year capped-price servicing totals $2,385 ($477 a year) on 12-month/20,000km intervals, with five years unlimited-km warranty, five years roadside assistance and an 8-year/160,000km battery warranty carrying a 70 per cent state-of-health guarantee

Equipment at the price includes a 36-inch head-up display, 16-inch touchscreen, 21-speaker audio, heated, ventilated and massaging front seats and tri-zone climate on the Long Range and above, and the 7X scored five stars under Euro NCAP with 91 per cent adult occupant protection
cons: The $75,900 Black Special Edition adds only cosmetics over the $72,900 Performance AWD - black wheels, black exterior trim and black Nappa leather, with no mechanical change - yet it is the one variant that sits above $75,000, so it loses the full novated-lease FBT exemption that applies to the rest of the range from 1 April 2027; a $3,000 styling pack that can cost several times that in lease terms

Adaptive air suspension on the Performance AWD and Black Special Edition is the biggest single criticism: CarExpert calls it flimsy at freeway speeds, bouncing dramatically over bumps as it auto-lowers, and explicitly recommends the steel-sprung Long Range RWD instead; Chasing Cars separately found front seats short on lateral support

Powered doors are called unreliable by both CarExpert and Chasing Cars - they misbehave on steep driveways and CarExpert raises a finger-pinch concern - and almost every function including climate control sits in the 16-inch touchscreen with very few physical controls

Chasing Cars measured the Performance AWD at 18.1kWh/100km on the highway and 19.7kWh/100km around town against a 17.5kWh/100km WLTP claim, so plan on roughly 480-520km rather than 543km, and both it and CarExpert flag weak, noisy air-conditioning in Australian summer heat plus no spare wheel, only a repair kit

Resale is unquantified: Zeekr has only sold cars in Australia since 2024, and the sibling Zeekr X was repriced down $5,000-$10,000 in a single model year, so there is no evidence 7X list pricing will hold despite the 2,200 sales achieved by March 2026
